description: UI Bridge State Machine page — discover, design, and manage state machine configs with states, transitions, graph visualization, pathfinding, and export. Users connect to SDK-enabled apps to discover states via fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis, then work across six tabs: Discovery (SDK app connection, explore/record data collection, fingerprint-based state discovery, and save), Graph Editor (visual node-edge layout via dagre with drag-and-drop element reassignment), State View (list + detail panel via shared StateViewPanel), Transitions (list with detail panel via shared TransitionsPanel), Pathfinding (find optimal paths between states via shared PathfindingPanel), and Export (save to JSON file or load into runtime).

groups.name: Page Header and Config Selector
groups.description: The page header shows a Network icon and a dynamic title (the active config name, or 'UI Bridge States' when no config is selected). A config selector dropdown lets users pick an existing config (showing name and render count). A Refresh button reloads configs and active data, showing a spinning animation during loading.

assertions.description: The page displays 'UI Bridge States' in the header when no config is selected, or the active config's name when one is loaded
assertions.expected: When no config is selected, the h1 heading shows 'UI Bridge States'. When a config is loaded, it shows the config's name instead.

assertions.description: A config selector dropdown with a 'Select configuration...' placeholder option lists all saved configs with name and render count
A 'Refresh' button reloads configs and the active config data, with a spinning RefreshCw icon during loading and disabled state

Selecting a config from the dropdown loads it and resets the discovery state. Each option shows the config name and render count (e.g., 'My Config (12 renders)'). Selecting the empty option clears the active config.
assertions.expected: Selecting a config option loads that config via loadConfig(), resets discovery state, and the page title updates to show the config name. Selecting the empty option clears the active config.

groups.name: Tab Navigation Bar
groups.description: Six tabs appear below the header: Discovery (Search icon), Graph Editor (GitBranch icon), State View (Layers icon), Transitions (ArrowRightLeft icon), Pathfinding (Route icon), and Export (Download icon). The active tab is highlighted with background and shadow styling. All tab panels stay in the DOM but are hidden when inactive.

assertions.description: The Discovery tab provides access to the SDK app connection and state discovery workflow
The Graph Editor tab provides access to the interactive dagre-based node-edge visualization with drag-and-drop element reassignment
The State View tab shows a list view of all states with detail panel
The Transitions tab lists all transitions between states with editing support
The Pathfinding tab enables users to find optimal paths between states
The Export tab provides JSON file export and runtime loading operations
Exactly 6 tabs are rendered in the tab bar
assertions.expected: The tab bar below the header should contain exactly 6 tab buttons: Discovery, Graph Editor, State View, Transitions, Pathfinding, Export

groups.name: Per-Tab Empty States (No Config Selected)
groups.description: When no config is selected, each content tab (except Discovery) shows a centered instructional message. The Graph Editor also shows a loading spinner when data is being fetched. Discovery works independently of config selection since it creates configs.

assertions.description: When no config is selected and not loading, the Graph Editor tab shows 'Select a configuration to view the state graph'

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to view the state graph

assertions.description: When no config is selected, the State View tab shows 'Select a configuration to view states'

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to view states

assertions.description: When no config is selected, the Transitions tab shows 'Select a configuration to view transitions'

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to view transitions

assertions.description: When no config is selected, the Pathfinding tab shows 'Select a configuration to use pathfinding'

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to use pathfinding

assertions.description: When no config is selected, the Export tab shows 'Select a configuration to export'

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Connect to SDK App
groups.description: Phase 1 of discovery. A 'Connect to SDK App' card with a Plug icon lets users scan for SDK-enabled apps. A 'Scan for Apps' button triggers web and desktop app scanning via useAppDiscovery. Discovered apps are listed with name, URL, framework, and a 'Connect' button. Once connected, a green banner shows the connected app name and the app list is hidden.

assertions.description: The connection card shows a 'Connect to SDK App' label with a Plug icon
preconditions: No co-occurrence data has been collected

assertions.description: A 'Scan for Apps' button triggers discovery of SDK-enabled web and desktop apps, showing a Loader2 spinner while scanning
preconditions: No co-occurrence data has been collected

assertions.description: After scanning, discovered apps are listed with app name, URL, framework info, and a 'Connect' button per app. A count label shows 'N app(s) found'.
assertions.expected: Each discovered app card shows: app name (font-medium), URL and framework in text-muted, and a 'Connect' button (brand-primary background). After connecting, the app list is hidden and replaced by a connected banner.

assertions.description: Once connected to an app, a green banner shows 'Connected: <app name>' with a CheckCircle2 icon, and the app list is hidden
assertions.expected: A green-tinted banner (bg-green-500/10, border-green-500/20) should appear with a CheckCircle2 icon and text 'Connected: <bold app name>'. The discovered apps list should be hidden.

assertions.description: When no apps are found and not scanning, instructional text says 'Click Scan to find apps with the UI Bridge SDK installed.'

criteria.textContent: Click Scan to find apps with the UI Bridge SDK installed.

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Data Collection (Explore/Record)
groups.description: Phase 2 of discovery, shown only when connected to an SDK app. Two sub-tabs: 'Explore' (automated exploration via sdk.exploreStates) and 'Record' (manual capture session via sdk.startCaptureSession/stopCaptureSession). Explore shows a 'Start Exploration' button with progress indicators. Record shows 'Start Recording'/'Stop Recording' buttons with capture count and unique fingerprint count.

assertions.description: An 'Explore' sub-tab with a Compass icon is available for automated state exploration
A 'Record' sub-tab with a Camera icon is available for manual capture sessions

The Explore sub-tab has a 'Start Exploration' button that triggers automated exploration. While exploring, it shows 'Exploring...' with a spinner and a 'Cancel' button appears. Progress is shown as 'current / total interactions' with the current element being explored.
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Start Exploration' begins automated exploration. The button text changes to 'Exploring...' with a Loader2 spinner and becomes disabled. A 'Cancel' button appears alongside. Progress text shows 'Progress: X / Y interactions' and 'Current: <element name>'. When exploration completes, co-occurrence data is stored and the view advances to Phase 3.

assertions.description: The Record sub-tab has 'Start Recording' and 'Stop Recording' buttons, plus capture count and unique fingerprint count displayed during/after recording
assertions.expected: Initially shows 'Start Recording' button with a red Circle icon. When recording, the button changes to 'Stop Recording' (red background, Square icon). A recording status area shows: a red pulsing dot with 'N captures' badge, and 'N unique fingerprints' text. Stopping recording generates co-occurrence export data and advances to Phase 3.

assertions.description: The Explore sub-tab shows explanatory text about automatic exploration by interacting with UI elements
assertions.expected: Automatically explore

groups.name: Discovery Tab: State Discovery and Save
groups.description: Phases 3 and 4 of discovery, shown after co-occurrence data is collected. First shows a data summary card ('Co-occurrence Data Collected') with capture count, fingerprint count, and data source. A 'Discover States' button runs fingerprint-based discovery. After discovery, results show state count, fingerprint count, capture count, a state preview list with names and confidence percentages, and a save form with a 'Configuration Name' input and 'Save Configuration' button.

assertions.description: A 'Co-occurrence Data Collected' card shows capture count, fingerprint count, and data source (explore/record) with a 'Start Over' reset button
A 'Start Over' button with a RotateCcw icon resets the discovery workflow back to the connect phase
A 'Discover States' button with a Sparkles icon runs fingerprint-based state discovery on the collected co-occurrence data
preconditions: Discovery has not been run yet

assertions.description: After discovery completes, a 'Discovery Complete' section shows state count, fingerprint count, and capture count badges. A scrollable state preview list shows each discovered state name with its confidence percentage.
assertions.expected: A card with green CheckCircle2 icon and 'Discovery Complete' heading should display: three badges showing 'N states', 'N fingerprints', 'N captures'. Below, a scrollable list (max-h-40) shows each state with its name on the left and 'X% confidence' on the right.

assertions.description: A 'Configuration Name' labeled input with placeholder 'e.g., My App States' allows naming the config before saving

A 'Save Configuration' button saves the discovered states as a new config. Disabled when the name is empty or saving is in progress. On success, switches to Graph Editor tab with the new config loaded.
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Save Configuration' calls discovery.saveConfig() which creates a new state machine config from the discovered states. The button is disabled (opacity-50) when the config name is empty or while saving. On success, the page switches to the Graph Editor tab with the newly created config loaded and selected.

groups.name: Discovery Algorithm Correctness
groups.description: The fingerprint-based state discovery algorithm processes co-occurrence data (presence matrix of element fingerprints across captures) to identify distinct UI states. Each discovered state has a unique fingerprint set and a confidence score. The correctness of the algorithm is verifiable by examining the state preview list in the discovery results.

assertions.description: Every discovered state in the preview list should have at least one element (non-empty elementIds). A state with zero elements indicates a grouping error in the discovery algorithm.
assertions.expected: Each state in the preview list should have a non-zero confidence value, indicating it was derived from at least one fingerprint. States with 0% confidence would indicate empty or invalid groupings.

assertions.description: No two discovered states should represent the same element configuration. Each state in the preview list should have a unique name and distinct confidence value, reflecting different fingerprint groupings.
assertions.expected: All state names in the preview list should be distinct. If two states have identical names and confidence values, it indicates the discovery algorithm failed to merge duplicate states.

assertions.description: The displayed statistics (state count, fingerprint count, capture count) should be internally consistent. The fingerprint count should be >= the state count (since multiple fingerprints can map to one state). The capture count should be >= the fingerprint count.
assertions.expected: The three badge values should satisfy: capture count >= fingerprint count >= state count. The state count badge should match the number of items in the state preview list.

groups.name: Graph Editor Tab Content
groups.description: The Graph Editor tab renders an interactive node-edge graph using @xyflow/react with dagre layout (via the shared StateMachineGraphView component). States are nodes and transitions are directed edges. A floating 'Add Transition' button in the top-left allows creating new transitions. Clicking a node selects a state; clicking an edge selects a transition. An empty graph shows a message guiding users to the Discovery tab. Elements can be dragged between nodes.

assertions.description: A floating 'Add Transition' button in the top-left of the graph tab allows users to create a new transition, opening the transition editor in the side panel
When no states exist, the graph shows 'No states discovered yet. Use the Discovery tab to discover states.' guiding users to the Discovery tab
assertions.expected: No states discovered yet
preconditions: A config is selected with zero states

assertions.description: Clicking a state node in the graph selects it and opens the state detail side panel, deselecting any previously selected transition
assertions.expected: Clicking a state node should: (1) highlight the node, (2) open the StateDetailPanel in the right side panel showing 'State Details' header, (3) deselect any previously selected transition and close the transition editor
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one state

assertions.description: Clicking a transition edge in the graph selects it and opens the transition editor side panel
assertions.expected: Clicking a transition edge should: (1) select the edge, (2) open the TransitionEditor in the right side panel in edit mode showing 'Edit Transition' header, (3) deselect any previously selected state
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one transition

assertions.description: Elements can be dragged between state nodes on the graph. Normal drag creates a transition between source and target states. Alt+drag moves the element from source to target state.
assertions.expected: Dragging an element tile from one state node to another should: without Alt key, create a new transition between the two states; with Alt key held, move the element from the source state to the target state. Drop targets are highlighted during drag.
preconditions: A config is selected with at least two states

assertions.description: A loading spinner appears in the graph area during async operations (config loading)
assertions.expected: When sm.isLoading is true, a centered Loader2 spinner (brand-primary color) should be displayed in the graph area instead of the graph canvas or empty message.

groups.name: Graph Visualization Controls
groups.description: The graph canvas has control buttons in the top-right (Fit, keyboard shortcut toggle, Re-layout), a stats panel in the bottom-left (state count, transition count, initial state name), a MiniMap, and keyboard shortcuts. Nodes display element grids, badges (START for initial, outgoing/incoming counts), and confidence indicators.

assertions.description: A 'Fit' button in the top-right controls panel adjusts the viewport to show all nodes
assertions.expected: The graph canvas should have a 'Fit' button (with Maximize icon) in the top-right Panel that fits all nodes into view when clicked. Keyboard shortcut 'F' also triggers this.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: A 'Re-layout' button in the top-right controls re-runs the dagre automatic layout algorithm
assertions.expected: The graph controls panel should include a 'Re-layout' button (with LayoutGrid icon) that recalculates node positions using dagre layout and fits the view. Keyboard shortcut 'L' also triggers this.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: A keyboard icon button toggles a 'Keyboard Shortcuts' overlay listing all available shortcuts including app-specific ones for drag-and-drop
assertions.expected: After clicking the keyboard icon button (or pressing '?'), a 'Keyboard Shortcuts' overlay should appear listing: Deselect all (Esc), Toggle shortcuts (?), Fit to view (F), Re-layout (L), Zoom in/out (+ / -), Cycle states (Tab), Jump to initial (I), Delete transition (Del), Create transition (Drag element), Move element (Alt+Drag)

assertions.description: A stats panel in the bottom-left shows state count, transition count, and the initial state name (in yellow with a Play icon)
assertions.expected: A semi-transparent panel in the bottom-left should show: 'N states | N transitions' and optionally '| <initial state name>' with a yellow Play icon if an initial state is set.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: State nodes display contextual badges: 'START' for the initial state (gold), outgoing transition count, incoming transition count, and 'no links' for disconnected states. Each node shows element count and confidence percentage.
assertions.expected: State nodes should show: a gold 'START' badge on the initial state, outgoing count badge, incoming count badge, and a 'no links' badge on disconnected states. Each node also shows element count and confidence percentage.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

groups.name: Graph Editor: State Detail Side Panel
groups.description: When a state is selected on the graph, a right side panel (w-80) opens with the shared StateDetailPanel component. It displays: 'State Details' header with a Close button, editable Name and Description fields, a 2x2 metadata grid (State ID, Confidence percentage, Elements count, Renders count), an editable Elements list with type-colored badges and add/remove capability, Acceptance Criteria (add/edit/remove), Domain Knowledge cards (add/remove), and Save Changes/Delete State buttons.

assertions.description: The state detail panel shows a 'State Details' header with a 'Close' button
The state detail panel shows an editable Name input field pre-filled with the selected state's name
assertions.expected: An editable Name text input should be pre-filled with the current state's name, allowing the user to rename the state. A 'Name' label appears above the input.

assertions.description: The state detail panel displays a 2x2 metadata grid showing State ID, Confidence percentage (color-coded), Elements count, and Renders count
assertions.expected: A 2-column grid should display: State ID (monospace code block), Confidence (color-coded percentage: green >= 80%, amber 50-79%, red < 50%), Elements count, and Renders count.

assertions.description: The state detail panel shows an Elements list with type-colored badges and the ability to add/remove elements via a 'type:element-id' input
assertions.expected: An 'Elements (N)' section lists each element with a type-colored badge (colored border and background based on element type). Each element has a hover-visible remove button. An 'Add' button and 'type:element-id' input allow adding new elements.
preconditions: A state is selected with elements

assertions.description: The state detail panel shows Acceptance Criteria with inline editing, add, and remove capabilities
assertions.expected: An 'Acceptance Criteria (N)' section lists each criterion as clickable text (click to edit inline). Each has a hover-visible remove button. An input with placeholder 'Add acceptance criterion...' and an 'Add' button allow adding new criteria.

assertions.description: The state detail panel provides 'Save Changes' and 'Delete State' buttons for persisting edits or removing the state
assertions.expected: A 'Save Changes' button (brand-primary, shown only when hasChanges is true) persists edits via onSave. A 'Delete State' button (red text/border) removes the state via onDelete. Both are disabled while saving.

groups.name: Graph Editor: Transition Editor Side Panel
groups.description: When a transition is selected or 'Add Transition' is clicked, a right side panel (w-80) opens with the shared TransitionEditor component. It shows 'Edit Transition' (editing) or 'New Transition' (creating) header with a Close button. The editor provides: name input, three state toggle groups (From States blue, Activate States green, Exit States red), action list with type-specific parameter fields, path cost, stays-visible checkbox, and Create/Update/Delete buttons.

assertions.description: The transition editor shows 'Edit Transition' when editing an existing transition or 'New Transition' when creating a new one, with a Close button
assertions.expected: The heading shows 'Edit Transition' when a transition is selected, or 'New Transition' when 'Add Transition' was clicked. A 'Close' text button dismisses the panel.
preconditions: Transition editor side panel is open

assertions.description: The transition editor shows three state toggle groups: 'From States' (blue), 'Activate States' (green), and 'Exit States' (red), each rendering toggleable buttons for available states
assertions.expected: Three labeled toggle groups should be visible: 'From States' (blue-500 accent when active), 'Activate States' (green-500 accent when active), and 'Exit States' (red-500 accent when active). Each group shows state names as toggleable buttons. When no states exist, shows 'No states' italic text.

assertions.description: The transition editor has an Actions section with '+ Add Action' button and action fields with type dropdown and type-specific parameter fields
assertions.expected: An 'Actions' label with '+ Add Action' button. Each action has: a type dropdown (Click, Double Click, Right Click, Type, Clear, Select, Focus, Blur, Hover, Scroll, Check, Uncheck, Toggle, Set Value, Drag, Submit, Reset, Wait, Navigate) with conditional fields: target element ID for click-like actions, target + text + 'Clear first' checkbox for type actions, URL for navigate, delay_ms for wait, direction + amount for scroll, source + target for drag.

assertions.description: The transition editor has 'Path Cost' number input and 'Stays Visible' checkbox options
assertions.expected: A 'Path Cost' number input (min 0, step 0.1, default 1.0) and a 'Stays Visible' checkbox should be present below the actions section.

assertions.description: The transition editor has a 'Create' button (new mode) or 'Update' button (edit mode) and a 'Delete' button (edit mode only)
assertions.expected: In create mode: a 'Create' button (brand-primary). In edit mode: an 'Update' button (brand-primary) and a 'Delete' button (red text/border). The Create/Update button is disabled when the transition name is empty or while saving.

groups.name: State View Tab Content
groups.description: The State View tab renders the shared StateViewPanel component (from @qontinui/workflow-ui/state-machine) which displays states in a list view with a detail panel. When no config is selected, shows an empty message.

assertions.description: The StateViewPanel component renders with the current config's states and transitions when a config is selected
assertions.expected: The StateViewPanel should render showing the list of states from the active config. Each state should be clickable to view details.

assertions.description: State selection in the State View tab syncs with the page-level state, so selecting a state here also deselects any transition
assertions.expected: Clicking a state in the StateViewPanel calls onSelectState, which sets the page-level selectedStateId and clears selectedTransitionId. This means switching to the Graph Editor tab would show the same state selected.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

groups.name: Transitions Tab Content
groups.description: The Transitions tab renders the shared TransitionsPanel component (from @qontinui/workflow-ui/state-machine) which displays transitions with editing support. When no config is selected, shows an empty message.

assertions.description: The TransitionsPanel component renders with the current config's states and transitions when a config is selected
assertions.expected: The TransitionsPanel should render showing the list of transitions from the active config. Each transition should be clickable to select it.

assertions.description: Transition selection in the Transitions tab syncs with the page-level state, so selecting a transition here also deselects any state
assertions.expected: Clicking a transition in the TransitionsPanel calls onSelectTransition, which sets the page-level selectedTransitionId and clears selectedStateId.
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

groups.name: Pathfinding Tab Content
groups.description: The Pathfinding tab renders the shared PathfindingPanel component (from @qontinui/workflow-ui/state-machine). Users select from/to states and an algorithm, then find paths. Successful paths are also highlighted on the Graph Editor tab via the highlightedPath prop.

assertions.description: The PathfindingPanel component renders with the current config's states and transitions when a config is selected
assertions.expected: The PathfindingPanel should render with from/to state selectors, algorithm choice, and a 'Find Path' button.

assertions.description: When a path is found, it is highlighted on the Graph Editor tab via the highlightedPath prop, showing the path edges in a distinct color
assertions.expected: After finding a path with result.found === true, switching to the Graph Editor tab should show the path edges highlighted. If no path is found, highlightedPath is cleared.
preconditions: A config is selected with states and transitions

assertions.description: After finding a path, the PathfindingPanel shows the result including step count, total cost, and step-by-step navigation through states via transitions
assertions.expected: After clicking 'Find Path': (1) Success: shows path found with step count and total cost, listing each step with transition name and from-to states. (2) Same state: indicates already at target. (3) No path: shows no path found message.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

groups.name: Export Tab
groups.description: The Export tab provides two operations: 'Save to File' (exports the config as JSON compatible with UIBridgeRuntime.from_dict() via Tauri's save dialog) and 'Load into Runtime' (POSTs the export data to /state-machine/load API endpoint). Shows config name, state count, and transition count. Uses toast notifications for success/error feedback.

assertions.description: The export panel shows an 'Export' heading with a FileJson icon
A 'Save to File' button exports the config as a JSON file through Tauri's save dialog, with a Download icon
A 'Load into Runtime' button POSTs the exported config to the /state-machine/load API endpoint, with an Upload icon
The export panel displays the current config name, state count, and transition count
assertions.expected: The export panel should show: 'Config: <config name>' in bold, 'N states' on one line, 'N transitions' on another line.

assertions.description: Clicking 'Save to File' opens Tauri's save dialog with a default filename based on the config name, and shows a success/error toast after completion
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Save to File' calls buildExportConfig to create JSON compatible with UIBridgeRuntime.from_dict(), then opens Tauri's save dialog with default filename '<config_name>_state_machine.json'. On success, shows 'Exported to <path>' toast. On failure, shows 'Export failed: <error>' toast. Button is disabled during export.

assertions.description: Clicking 'Load into Runtime' POSTs the export data to the API and shows a success/error toast
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Load into Runtime' POSTs the buildExportConfig result to /state-machine/load. On success, shows 'State machine loaded into runtime' toast. On failure, shows 'Load failed: <error>' toast. Button is disabled during load and while export is in progress.

groups.name: Toast Notifications
groups.description: The page uses a toast notification system (useToast + ToastContainer) for user feedback throughout all operations. Toasts appear for export success/failure, runtime load success/failure, discovery save success, and other operations.

assertions.description: A ToastContainer component is rendered at the page level to display toast notifications from all operations
assertions.expected: A ToastContainer should be present at the bottom of the page layout, receiving toasts from the useToast hook and rendering them with dismiss capability.

assertions.description: Export operations show success or error toasts with descriptive messages
assertions.expected: After a successful export: a success toast with 'Exported to <path>'. After a failed export: an error toast with 'Export failed: <error>'. After successful runtime load: 'State machine loaded into runtime'. After failed load: 'Load failed: <error>'.
preconditions: An export or load operation has completed
